correctness.rationale: Exact change z=x-y, v=z-dot conjugates the planar logit field to z-double-dot+f(z)z-dot+g(z)=0 with f=1-(lambda/4)sech^2(lambda*z/2) and g=(alpha/2)tanh(lambda*z/2). Direct differentiation checks the map and restoring force. For lambda<=4, proper energy E=v^2/2+(alpha/lambda)log cosh(lambda*z/2) decreases, and the only invariant subset with f(z)*v^2=0 is the origin; LaSalle includes equality lambda=4. For lambda>4, odd F=integral f has unique positive crossing, is increasing thereafter, and g is odd positive for z>0 with coercive potential; classical Lienard uniqueness yields one attracting nonconstant orbit. Logistic reflection fixes its half-period average. Taylor f=-delta/4+4z^2+O(delta*z^2+z^4), g=alpha*z+O(delta*z+z^3), and averaging <sin^2>=1/2, <sin^2 cos^2>=1/8 yield A-dot=delta A/8-A^3/2+higher terms, so the Hopf amplitude satisfies A^2=delta/4+O(delta^2) and T->2pi/sqrt(alpha). The exact inverse x=(S_lambda(z)+alpha/2-v)/(1+alpha), y=x-z gives centered x and y amplitudes 1/(2sqrt(1+alpha)) and sqrt(alpha)/(2sqrt(1+alpha)), respectively. Independent SymPy verification checked f,g and critical z^2 coefficient 4; finite simulation is not treated as the all-parameter proof.
